claims.text: Defense customers generated $5.9B, ~49% of revenue in FY2025 (vs $5.1B / ~47% in FY2024). Key defense customers include all six branches of the U.S. military, OSD, NASA and the Joint Staff.
Intelligence customers generated $1.9B, ~16% of revenue in FY2025 (vs $1.8B / ~17% in FY2024) across the 18 organizations of the U.S. Intelligence Community including NSA and DIA.
Civil and global commercial customers generated $4.2B, ~35% of revenue in FY2025 (vs $3.8B / ~36% in FY2024); commercial cyber is 2% of total revenue.
Approximately 85% of FY2025 revenue was derived from 2,596 active task orders under IDIQ contract vehicles.
The top IDIQ contract vehicle represented approximately 18% of FY2025 revenue.
The largest task order under an IDIQ contract vehicle accounted for approximately 4% of FY2025 revenue.
As of March 31, 2025 Booz Allen has 35,800 employees (32,700 customer staff); approximately 72% of employees hold security clearances (~25,776 cleared).
Total backlog grew 15% YoY to $37.0B as of March 31, 2025 ($32.1B prior); funded backlog $5.7B (incl PGSC acquisition $231M); priced options $23.8B. Additions to funded backlog were $12.2B in FY2025.

BAH's national security intelligence work explicitly supports 'national cyber mission providers' including NSA and DIA, with revenue routed through cleared workforce; cyber mission customer mix is a stated forward growth driver.

The 2025 Appropriations Act (signed March 15, 2025) funds the U.S. government under a continuing resolution through September 30, 2025; total CR funding is roughly equivalent to FY2024 with DoD base budget increased and nondefense spending reduced; DoD given conditional authority for new program starts.

The new U.S. administration's spending-review Executive Orders have already led to BAH contracts being 'impacted, reduced or canceled' and to price adjustments/renegotiations prior to option exercise; agency personnel reductions have slowed procurement and clearance processing.
BAH carries a $245M liability for DCAA-claimed-cost adjustments covering fiscal years subsequent to 2011; DCMA has been increasing the proportion of executive compensation deemed unallowable.
